name: OpenAIGPTLive
title: OpenAI GPT-Live
whenToUse: Pick when someone should TALK to the workflow and be spoken back to naturally, with the model listening while it speaks, handling pauses and interruptions, and keeping the conversation going while slower work runs behind it. Reading a script word for word, and transcribing a recording that already exists, are different jobs. Tools come from MCP provider nodes attached via service edges.

inputs.name: input
inputs.description: The task, at the start and whenever it changes

inputs.name: answer
inputs.description: The backend's answer, for it to say

outputs.name: transcript
outputs.description: The whole call, when it ends

systemPrompt.title: System Prompt
systemPrompt.description: How the model should behave on the call. Shared blocks work here.

voice.title: Voice
voice.description: Which voice the model speaks with. Fixed for the length of the call.

initialRequest.title: Opening
initialRequest.description: What the model should say first, the moment the call opens. Leave empty and it waits for the person.

conversationHistory.title: Conversation History
conversationHistory.description: Prior turns to start from, as an array of { role, content }. Up to 128 messages and 8,192 tokens, text only.

delegation.title: Hands work to
delegation.description: Who answers what the voice cannot.

backendPrompt.title: Thinking model's instructions
backendPrompt.description: How the model behind the voice should work.

backendTools.title: Tools
backendTools.description: Function definitions the thinking model may call.

lane.title: Lane
lane.description: Where the audio comes from and goes to. Browser is this page's microphone. Clip a phone line onto this node to put the conversation on a real number instead.

authRequired.title: Require sign-in
authRequired.description: Only a signed-in caller may run this step. Leave off and it runs for whoever the workflow's trigger admitted, which is the usual answer.

authRole.title: Require role
authRole.description: A claim the caller's account must carry, as noun:verb (finance:approve, payments:refund). Leave blank to require only that they are signed in.

package.name: openai
package.packageFile:
# The package envelope, and now the ONLY envelope: this package is fully
# declarative. All five nodes are manifests, there is no src/ and no package.json,
# so nothing here is built, published or imported. The retired TypeScript sits at
# _legacy/nodes/openai for reference.
#
# A code node of the same type always beats a manifest at load, which is what made
# migrating one node at a time possible. With the code gone there is nothing left
# to beat these.

name: openai
displayName: OpenAI
description: OpenAI integration for Unoverse
version: 1.3.0
category: ai
# First-party. The marketplace shows this on every node the package registers, so
# "who am I trusting with this credential" is answerable without leaving the screen.
publisher: unoverse
logoUrl: https://res.cloudinary.com/sonik/image/upload/v1749262616/gravity/icons/ChatGPT-Logo.svg.webp

features:
  - GPT-5.6 models
  - Live two-way voice, with the model interruptible mid-sentence
  - Streaming responses
  - Function/tool calling
  - Text embeddings
  - Structured JSON output
  - Vision (image inputs)
  - Realtime voice calls with transcripts of both sides
  - Search detail, one question answered by opening one branch of a tree at a time

# The ONLY hosts this package's nodes may call. The executor refuses anything else.
#
# A manifest cannot execute code, but without this it could still say "send this
# credential to evil.example", which is exfiltration with no code at all. One short
# reviewable list is what makes a manifest safe to accept from someone else.
allowedHosts:
  - api.openai.com
  # LOOPBACK, numeric form: OpenAISearchDetail reads the choices one step from a row from the
  # platform's own engine over `scope.engineUrl` (127.0.0.1:4101), the same declaration the
  # ingest and spatial packages carry. It sends the engine ids, never the credential.
  - 127.0.0.1

# Executor capabilities every manifest node here depends on. Deploy REFUSES this
# package if the target universe's executor cannot satisfy them, so a manifest can
# never name a capability that only exists on a newer executor.
# `ws` and the raised floor came with OpenAIRealtimeVoice (2026-08-12): a realtime session is a
# SOCKET, and the duplex runtime that holds one open landed in executor 1.5.0.
requires:
  credential: [bearer]
  transport: [sse, json, ws]
  # OpenAIAgent keeps its OpenAI conversation id between runs. A universe whose executor
  # cannot do this would otherwise read a permanently cold cache and start a new
  # conversation every turn: memory that silently never remembers.
  state: [read, merge]
  # OpenAISearchDetail walks in turns (`repeat`), each built from the reply before.
  repeat: true
  executorVersion: ">=1.5.0"

credentials.openAICredential.yaml:
# The SHAPE of the credential, never its value. Transcribed from
# plugin-base/src/credentials/openai.ts, which this package re-exports today.
#
# Values live where they already live: encrypted in Postgres on a deployed universe,
# and in the developer's own .env locally. That is why a manifest is safe to commit.
#
# Nodes reference this by NAME. At run time context.credentials holds EVERY credential
# in the workflow keyed by name, and the executor must select by name, never by
# scanning for the first object with an apiKey: openAICredential, apolloCredential,
# hunterCredential and searchapiCredential all expose one, so a scan silently
# authenticates against the wrong service the moment a second is added to the
# workflow (04-credentials.md).

name: openAICredential
displayName: OpenAI
description: Credentials for OpenAI API
documentationUrl: https://platform.openai.com/api-keys

properties:
  - name: apiKey
    displayName: API Key
    type: string
    required: true
    secret: true
    description: Your OpenAI API key
    placeholder: sk-...

  - name: organizationId
    displayName: Organization ID
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: Your OpenAI organization ID (optional)
    placeholder: org-...

  - name: baseUrl
    displayName: Base URL
    type: string
    required: false
    secret: false
    description: Custom API endpoint (optional)
    default: https://api.openai.com/v1

shared.endpoints.yaml:
# OpenAI's endpoints. Written once here rather than seven times across the nodes.
#
# No chat/completions: every node uses the Responses API. `messages` is the legacy shape.
#
#   url: { $ref: ../../shared/endpoints.yaml#/responses }

responses: https://api.openai.com/v1/responses
embeddings: https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings

# A CONVERSATION is OpenAI's own server-side memory: a durable id you mint once and then
# name on every response. Items are prepended to the request and the turn's input and
# output are appended back, so history never travels from here and is never stored here.
# Minted with POST and an empty body; the reply carries the id.
#
# NO CALLER SINCE 2026-08-23. OpenAIAgent was the only one and now chains with
# previous_response_id instead. Kept because the URL is a fact about the vendor rather
# than about any node, and re-deriving it is the sort of small cost that argues for
# leaving a one-line constant alone. Nothing here decides which mechanism a node uses —
# each declares that next to its own reason (shared/tools.yaml).
conversations: https://api.openai.com/v1/conversations
shared.models.yaml:
# The canonical GPT model list, the SINGLE source every OpenAI node references,
# organised by TIER. Transcribed from src/shared/models.ts.
#
# Models come in three tiers. A new generation is a one-line edit per tier here, and
# every node plus every saved workflow moves over automatically.
#
# The DATA lives here. The FALLBACK LOGIC (resolveModel: a retired id resolves to the
# current best model in its tier, so replacing a generation cannot break a saved
# workflow) is computation, not description, so it belongs to the executor. It is
# declared per config field as `resolver: modelTier`, not written here.

# One current model per tier. Update these three lines when a new generation ships.
byTier:
  small: gpt-5.6-luna # cost-optimized, high-volume
  medium: gpt-5.6-terra # balanced intelligence/cost, the default
  large: gpt-5.6 # frontier, complex work

# Balanced middle tier, the sensible default for most work.
default: gpt-5.6-terra

# The NARRATOR: the model that writes an agent's short "thinking" status line. A separate
# concern from the model doing the work, so it is named separately.
#
# Deliberately NOT the 5.6 family: 5.6 is luna/sol/terra with no nano tier, and this call
# exists to reach the user fast, not to be clever. Measured 2026-07-26, three runs each,
# same prompt and schema:
#
#   gpt-5.4-nano   avg 1137ms   [1470, 905, 1035]
#   gpt-5.6-luna   avg 2043ms   [1846, 2337, 1945]
#
# Luna is ~80% slower and less consistent for lines that are indistinguishable in quality.
# Re-measure when a faster small model ships; never assume.
narrator: gpt-5.4-nano


# The picker's options. Listed large first so the strongest reads first.
enum:
  - gpt-5.6
  - gpt-5.6-terra
  - gpt-5.6-luna

enumNames:
  - Sol (Frontier, complex work)
  - Terra (Balanced intelligence/cost)
  - Luna (Cost-optimized, high-volume)
shared.realtimeTools.yaml:
# The OpenAI REALTIME tool protocol.
#
# Vendor-specific, so it does not belong in the platform runtime. Node-agnostic, so it does not
# belong copied into a node either. It belongs here, exactly as `openai/shared/tools.yaml` holds the
# Responses protocol — imported whole:
#
#   toolExchange:
#     $ref: ../../shared/tools.yaml
#
# WHY THIS IS NOT `openai/shared/tools.yaml`. Same vendor, different API, and three real differences
# rather than cosmetic ones:
#
#   the call event   Responses says `response.output_item.done` and needs a `when` to tell a function
#                    call from any other completed item. Realtime has a dedicated
#                    `response.function_call_arguments.done`, so no `when` is needed.
#   offer, not      Responses puts the tool list in each REQUEST, so a list that GREW since the
#   toolsInto       last turn is re-sent for free and there is nothing to declare. A socket sends
#                   it once at the handshake, so growth has to be announced on purpose — which is
#                   what `offer` below is. Same fact, two shapes: `toolsInto` names a request
#                   field, `offer` names a whole message.
#   no continuity    Responses chains turns with previous_response_id. THE SOCKET IS THE CONTINUITY:
#                    the conversation never ended, so there is nothing to chain.
#
# Also absent, and deliberately: `maxTurns` and `stuckAfterRepeats`. Both count turns, and a turn is
# one model call. Nothing to count here. What bounds a runaway session is the executor's own idle and
# duration ceiling.

# How ONE tool is offered. `tool` is { name, description, parameters }.
tool: >-
  return { type: 'function', name: tool.name, description: tool.description,
           parameters: tool.parameters }

# HOW THE LIST IS RE-OFFERED once it has grown. `tools` is the whole live list, already in the
# envelope `tool` above produces.
#
# ONLY `tools`: session.update MERGES (verified live 2026-08-12), so instructions, modalities,
# voice and turn detection survive untouched. Re-sending the whole session block would be a second
# copy of the handshake, free to drift. Safe at any moment — the vendor gates `response.create` on
# an idle conversation, never session.update.
offer: >-
  return { type: 'session.update', session: { type: 'realtime', tools: tools } }

# HOW THE INSTRUCTIONS ARE RE-SENT when a region skill comes into force or is cleared.
#
# The same shape and the same reason as `offer` above, for the other thing the handshake sent
# once. A request/response vendor rebuilds its prompt every turn, so a skill absorbed on one
# turn is in the next request for free and there is nothing to declare. A socket sent
# `instructions` at the handshake and would otherwise never mention it again, so the model
# would keep working to a prompt that no longer describes where the conversation is.
#
# ONLY `instructions`: session.update MERGES, so voice, modalities, tools and turn detection
# survive untouched. `skillsText` is the platform's rendering of what is in force — it decides
# WHICH skills apply, this decides where the vendor puts them.
#
# The config prompt is repeated rather than sent alone, because a merge REPLACES the field it
# names: sending only the skills would drop the role the node was configured with.
reinstruct: >-
  return { type: 'session.update',
           session: { type: 'realtime',
                      instructions: config.systemPrompt + skillsText } }

# How a call ARRIVES. `match` is what makes a stream tractable: events keep coming for the whole
# conversation, and this says which of them is a tool call rather than a transcript or audio.
call:
  match: response.function_call_arguments.done
  id: "return response.call_id"
  name: "return response.name"
  # A JSON STRING, which the executor parses. The trap the schema warns about: passed through
  # unparsed, the tool receives a string where it expected its parameters.
  arguments: "return response.arguments"

# How the result goes BACK. TWO messages, because OpenAI separates them: the output joins the
# conversation, then a response is asked for. Without the second the model holds the result silently.
result: >-
  return [
    { type: 'conversation.item.create',
      item: { type: 'function_call_output', call_id: call.id, output: call.output } },
    { type: 'response.create' }
  ]
shared.task.yaml:
# THE TASK A CALL WAS GIVEN, FOUND RATHER THAN NAMED.
#
# A voice node is wired to whatever the canvas put upstream, so it cannot know the sending
# node's id or the name of the output handle. What it does know is the SHAPE: a task carries a
# list of `fields` still outstanding. So every wired value is looked at and the one with that
# shape is the task.
#
# THREE LEVELS, because a wired input arrives nested and how deep depends on the wiring:
# `signal.<input handle>.<sending node>.<its output>`. Measured 2026-09-22: written to look two
# levels down it found nothing at all, the call opened with no brief and no record_answers tool,
# and the model invented a customer's name on a live call rather than reading the one it held.

helpers:
  briefIn:
    args: [signal]
    body: >-
      return (() => {
        const flat = o => (o && typeof o === 'object' && !Array.isArray(o)) ? Object.values(o) : [];
        const l1 = flat(signal);
        const l2 = l1.reduce((acc, v) => acc.concat(flat(v)), []);
        const l3 = l2.reduce((acc, v) => acc.concat(flat(v)), []);
        const found = l1.concat(l2).concat(l3)
          .map(v => (v && typeof v === 'object') ? (v.requirements || v) : null)
          .filter(r => r && Array.isArray(r.fields));
        return found.length ? found[0] : null;
      })()

  # THE NAMES ONLY. A task's `fields` are sometimes plain strings and sometimes objects with a
  # name; what a tool's enum needs is the words either way.
  fieldNamesIn:
    args: [brief]
    body: >-
      return ((brief || {}).fields || [])
        .map(f => (typeof f === 'string' ? f
          : String((f || {}).name || (f || {}).field || (f || {}).key || '')))
        .filter(n => n)
shared.tools.yaml:
# The OpenAI Responses tool protocol.
#
# Vendor-specific, so it does NOT belong in the platform runtime. Node-agnostic, so it
# does not belong copied into every node either. It belongs here: shared by every OpenAI
# node, imported whole.
#
#   toolExchange:
#     $ref: ../../shared/tools.yaml
#     maxTurns: 5            # local keys layer on top and win
#
# When OpenAI changes how a function call is expressed, exactly one file changes.
# NO SDK. This is the wire format, described as data.

# How ONE tool is offered to the model. `tool` is { name, description, parameters }.
#
# `strict: false`, said out loud. Left unsaid, the Responses API defaults it to true and
# REWRITES the schema to fit: every property joins `required`, and `minLength` is enforced by
# the decoder. A briefed component's contract is the opposite, `required: []`, "any subset is
# a valid call" (core/markdown/compile.ts). Under the default the model could not open a task
# without writing every field, so it asked the guest questions instead (SAB transfer,
# 2026-09-15, read back from the stored responses). The server referees each call anyway.
# `output_schema` when the tool declares what it returns (a component's `outputs` block, MCP
# `outputSchema`): the model reads what comes back before it calls.
tool: >-
  return { type: 'function', name: tool.name, description: tool.description,
           parameters: tool.parameters, strict: false,
           ...(tool.outputSchema ? { output_schema: tool.outputSchema } : {}) }
toolsInto: tools

# How a call ARRIVES in the stream.
call:
  match: response.output_item.done
  when: "return response.item.type === 'function_call'"
  id: "return response.item.call_id"
  name: "return response.item.name"
  arguments: "return response.item.arguments"

# How ONE result goes BACK. `call` is { id, name, output }.
result: >-
  return { type: 'function_call_output', call_id: call.id, output: call.output }
resultsInto: input

# Always auto: which tool to reach for is carried by the tool DESCRIPTIONS, never by
# forcing a choice.
choiceInto: tool_choice
choice: auto

# NO `continuity` HERE, and that is deliberate. How a turn reaches the one before it is a
# per-node CHOICE on this vendor, not one wire format, because OpenAI offers two and
# REFUSES both at once:
#
#   previous_response_id   chains response to response. A new id every turn, known only
#                          after the turn ends. Declared by OpenAIStream, and since
#                          2026-08-23 by OpenAIAgent too — which now outlives a single
#                          execution by REMEMBERING that id (continuity.remember) rather
#                          than by holding a durable one.
#   conversation           a durable id, minted once and named on every turn, with the API
#                          keeping the history. No caller today.
#
# Sending both is `mutually_exclusive_parameters`, a hard 400 (confirmed against the live
# API 2026-08-12). So a node that names a conversation must NOT inherit continuity, and
# this file cannot decide for both. Each declares its own, next to the reason it chose it.

files.api/audio.yaml:
# THE AUDIO LANE. The platform's socket to the browser, not the vendor's.
#
# This file exists for ONE reason: MCP cannot carry binary audio. Everything else this node
# produces is in events.yaml and reaches the client over MCP streaming.

in:
  resampleTo: 24000
  message:
    type: session.input_audio.append
    audio: "{{ audio.base64 }}"

out:
  match: session.output_audio.delta
  value: "return response.delta"
  # NO `done` AND NO `interruptOn`: GPT-Live sends no end-of-speech or speech-started event. The
  # model decides when to stop talking, so a person speaking never cuts its audio.

control:
  # THE MODEL HANGING UP. `endOn` below is the LANE's list and every entry means the PERSON
  # left; nothing there can say the assistant is finished, and GPT-Live sends no end-of-call
  # event. So a call whose business was done held the line in silence until the idle timer
  # fired (heard live, 2026-09-22). A tool named `end_call` is how it says so.
  endWhen: >-
    return response.type === 'response.event'
      && !!response.event
      && response.event.type === 'response.output_item.done'
      && !!response.event.item
      && response.event.item.type === 'function_call'
      && response.event.item.name === 'end_call'

  # The person pressing hang up. Runs the `close` list in api/run.yaml.
  endOn: [END_CALL, stop]
  # The call state's "thinking": a hand-off starts the backend's work, and the vendor's
  # acknowledgement of the answer (see the `send` rule in api/run.yaml) ends it.
  toolUse: session.delegation.created
  toolUseCompleted: session.commentary.appended
files.config.yaml:
configSchema:
  type: object
  required: [model, voice]
  properties:
    # Named in config, as the other voice node names its model, because the usage record reads the
    # model from here: GPT-Live's events never carry it, and an unnamed model cannot be priced.
    model:
      type: string
      title: Model
      description: The live voice model.
      enum: [gpt-live-1]
      enumNames: [GPT-Live 1]
      default: gpt-live-1
    systemPrompt:
      type: string
      title: System Prompt
      description: How the model should behave on the call. Shared blocks work here.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    voice:
      type: string
      title: Voice
      description: Which voice the model speaks with. Fixed for the length of the call.
      # GPT-Live's own twelve, by their API names (live-conversations guide). The Realtime voices
      # are a different set and are not offered here.
      enum: [gleam, meridian, quartz, ripple, vesper, willow, stone, delta, cinder, beacon, bossa, tempo]
      enumNames:
        - Gleam (North American, feminine)
        - Meridian (North American, masculine)
        - Quartz (Australian, feminine)
        - Ripple (Australian, masculine)
        - Vesper (British, masculine)
        - Willow (Irish, feminine)
        - Stone (Irish, masculine)
        - Delta (Southern U.S., feminine)
        - Cinder (Southern U.S., masculine)
        - Beacon (Filipino, masculine)
        - Bossa (Brazilian Portuguese, feminine)
        - Tempo (Brazilian Portuguese, masculine)
      default: gleam
    # No response.create exists to make GPT-Live speak first. The vendor's way is an instruction
    # telling it to greet now, so this field is worded as that instruction rather than as a user line.
    initialRequest:
      type: string
      title: Opening
      description: >-
        What the model should say first, the moment the call opens. Leave empty and it waits for
        the person.
      default: ""
      "ui:field": template
    conversationHistory:
      type: object
      title: Conversation History
      description: >-
        Prior turns to start from, as an array of { role, content }. Up to 128 messages and 8,192
        tokens, text only.
      "ui:field": template
    # THE LANE THIS CONVERSATION TRAVELS ON (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §14).
    #
    # Browser is the ordinary case and needs nothing: the page captures the microphone and plays
    # the reply back. Every other value is OWNED BY AN ATTACHMENT — clip a Twilio Phone Line onto
    # this node and it sets this field to `twilio` and greys it out here, because one value has
    # one owner.
    #
    # It is a plain config field rather than anything new, which is the point: this node does not
    # know what a phone is. It reads `lane` the way it reads `voice`, and the runtime picks the
    # audio lane that name refers to (VOICE_STREAMING_GUIDE.md, "The Phone Lane"). A sample rate
    # is not here for the same reason: the lane's rate is a fact of the lane, never a choice.
    # WHO THE VOICE HANDS WORK TO. GPT-Live talks and listens; it does not think, so every
    # question it cannot answer goes to a second model. This says whose.
    #
    # OUR AGENT (the vendor's `client` mode) hands off to whatever `task` is wired to on the
    # canvas: your own agent, your own tools, your own prompt, and you see every hand-off. The
    # cost is that the vendor's hand-off event carries NO task text, only an id, so what the
    # backend receives is reconstructed from the transcript.
    #
    # OPENAI (the vendor's `responses` mode) hands off to a model OpenAI runs, which can call
    # FUNCTION TOOLS. So a hand-off arrives named and typed, `record_field { field, value }`
    # rather than a guess at what was meant, and our own runtime still executes it. The cost is
    # that the canvas agent is no longer the backend: what it could do has to be declared below
    # as tools instead.
    delegation:
      type: string
      title: Hands work to
      description: Who answers what the voice cannot.
      enum: [client, responses]
      enumNames: ["Our agent, on the canvas", "OpenAI, with the tools below"]
      default: client

    # THE THINKING MODEL, when OpenAI is doing the thinking. Not the live model: that one talks,
    # this one reasons, and they are chosen separately.
    backendModel:
      type: string
      title: Thinking model
      description: The model behind the voice.
      enum: [gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-luna]
      enumNames: [Terra, Luna]
      default: gpt-5.6-terra
      ui:dependencies:
        delegation: responses

    backendPrompt:
      type: string
      title: Thinking model's instructions
      description: How the model behind the voice should work.
      default: ""
      ui:field: template
      ui:dependencies:
        delegation: responses

    # WHAT IT MAY DO, as function definitions. Our own runtime executes every one of them, so
    # this is not a way to give OpenAI reach: it is the list of things the voice can ask FOR,
    # and a name that is not here cannot be called.
    backendTools:
      type: object
      title: Tools
      description: Function definitions the thinking model may call.
      ui:field: template
      ui:dependencies:
        delegation: responses

    lane:
      type: string
      title: Lane
      description: >-
        Where the audio comes from and goes to. Browser is this page's microphone. Clip a phone
        line onto this node to put the conversation on a real number instead.
      enum: [browser, twilio]
      enumNames: [Browser, Twilio phone line]
      default: browser
"ui:order": [model, systemPrompt, voice, initialRequest, conversationHistory,
             delegation, backendModel, backendPrompt, backendTools, lane]
files.interface.yaml:
inputs:
  # THE TASK. The first time it opens the call; every time after it updates the standing
  # orders, because "here is the task" is ONE idea and whether it is the first or the fifth is
  # the runtime's business (CallbackNodeActor delivers a repeat to the running session).
  - name: input
    type: object
    description: The task, at the start and whenever it changes
    required: false

  # ARRIVES WHILE THE CALL RUNS. `CONTINUE` is what makes that possible: the value is handed to
  # the open call rather than starting the node again, which would open a second one. Wire the
  # backend's final answer here, not a stream: a stream sends the answer so far each time, and
  # the model would be told the same sentence over and over.
  - name: answer
    type: object
    signal: CONTINUE
    description: The backend's answer, for it to say
    required: false

outputs:
  - name: task
    type: object
    description: "A hand-off to the backend"
  - name: transcript
    type: string
    description: The whole call, when it ends

credentials:
  - name: openAICredential
    required: true
    displayName: OpenAI
files.node.yaml:
type: OpenAIGPTLive
kind: CallbackNode

name: OpenAI GPT-Live
category: Voice
color: "#10A37F"

description: Full-duplex voice conversation with GPT-Live-1

whenToUse: >-
  Pick when someone should TALK to the workflow and be spoken back to naturally, with the model
  listening while it speaks, handling pauses and interruptions, and keeping the conversation going
  while slower work runs behind it. Reading a script word for word, and transcribing a recording
  that already exists, are different jobs. Tools come from MCP provider nodes attached via service
  edges.

# WHO MAY RUN THIS (DECLARATIVE_NODES.md §9.13). Compulsory on every node, so that a node
# nobody thought about cannot look the same as one deliberately left open.
#
# `required: false` adds no requirement of its own: the node runs for whoever the trigger
# admitted. The trigger instance's publicEntry toggle still owns the door, and requirements
# only ever narrow.
auth:
  required: false

capabilities:
  # A live conversation is never cacheable: the answer depends on what was just said.
  cacheable: false
files.test.yaml:
# A duplex node cannot be proved by a fixture the way a request can: there is no single reply, and
# nobody is talking. This starts the session, asserts the vendor accepted it, and asserts the voice
# spoke its opening. `session.started` coming back proves the url, the key and every field in the
# session block were acceptable.
#
# The audio path and the tools need a real call, which `unoverse node test` cannot stand in for.

testData:
  config:
    model: gpt-live-1
    systemPrompt: You are on a test call. Keep every reply to one short sentence.
    voice: gleam
    initialRequest: Say the single word hello.
  inputs:
    input: {}
  expect:
    transcript: "return output.transcript.includes('Assistant:')"
